title: Claim set, v0
description:
One document's claims and the typed relations between them. This is the interchange form: a single JSON file that a consumer can read with no knowledge of how it was produced, of the authoring layout (claims/<doc>/*.md), or of any publisher. The authoring form is normalised into this on export; where the two disagree, this file is the contract.

The relation graph is directed, multi-edged and CYCLIC. Converse pairs are the reason (a hypothesis entails a prediction; the prediction tests the hypothesis), and `edges` stores each direction it was given. Consumers must not assume acyclicity. See `views` for the spanning-tree projections a reader UI can use instead.

document.description: What the claims are asserted in. A claim set has exactly one primary document; a claim may carry assertions in others (see claim.assertions).

license.description: SPDX id or URL for the source document, e.g. CC-BY-4.0.

provenance.description: How this set was produced. Required reading for anyone deciding how much to trust it.

reviewed.description: Whether a person has checked this set. `none` means every claim and edge is machine output that no human has verified.

sourceRun.description: Opaque pointer to the producing run, e.g. runs/<doc>/ledger.jsonl#<hash>.

questions.description: The questions the document sets out to answer. Claims point at these with `addresses`.

edges.description: Typed relations between claims. Directed; may contain cycles; may contain both directions of a converse pair. Duplicates of the same (from, rel, to) are not permitted.

views.description: Acyclic projections of the graph, for consumers that need a tree (a reader UI, an outline, a table of contents). A view is advisory: it carries no information the graph does not, and dropping it loses no claims.

follow.description: Which relations the projection walks, in preference order. The walk stops at the first already-visited node, which is what makes the result a tree.

localId.description: Lowercase kebab-case. Unique within its collection in this file.

claimRef.description: A claim: either a localId in this set, or `<document-id>:<claim-id>` for a claim in another set. A consumer that cannot resolve the document half should treat the edge as dangling rather than dropping it silently.

id.description: Stable within this set; the key a citing tool writes (tika's `claim=KEY`).

uuid.description: Stable across sets and across renames of `id`. Identity is the proposition, not the document: the same proposition asserted by two documents is ONE claim with two `assertions`.

text.description: The proposition, as one declarative sentence, in the document's own register.

plain.description: The same proposition for a non-specialist. One sentence, no statistics, no jargon.

short.description: Label length, for graph nodes and chips.

type.description: The claim's epistemic kind — what sort of thing it is. One axis only; see `function` for the other.

function.description: The claim's job in the argument, where that is not implied by `type`. `control` validates a method or rules out an artefact; `literature-context` is imported from another paper and not shown here; `alternative` is a rival explanation the document argues against (its assertion carries stance `rejects`).

confidence.description: How firmly the document asserts this, as judged at extraction. NOT a reproduction outcome — see `reproductions.status` for that, and note that `reviewed: none` makes this a machine judgement.

concepts.description: Free-text index terms. Not a controlled vocabulary and not load-bearing.

assertions.description: Where this proposition is asserted and on what grounds. More than one entry means the same claim is asserted by more than one document — the mechanism by which a claim outlives any single paper.

reproductions.description: Attempts to re-derive the claim's result from its data and code. Absent or empty means untried, which is not the same as failed.

document.description: Document id. The primary document appears here too.

stance.description: What this document does with the proposition. `asserts` is the default and by far the common case; `rejects` marks a rival explanation the document argues against — a claim it states in order to rule out.

locator.description: Where in the document. `panel` is the figure panel or analysis block that produced the result — the unit the whole format is built on.

quote.description: A sentence from the document that asserts it, verbatim.

grounds.description: What the claim rests on. Absent fields mean not recorded, never "none".

analysis.description: Path or URL to the script, e.g. scripts/Fig5.ipynb.

confidence.description: Per-document; overrides the claim-level value for this assertion.

status.description: `verified` re-derived the result. `mismatch` ran and disagreed — the only value that is a negative finding about the claim. `partial` ran and agreed in part. `blocked` could not run (see `blockedBy`). `unattempted` was never tried. `unverified` was tried and neither confirmed nor refuted.

by.description: Who or what ran it. An agent name here is NOT a person's check.

blockedBy.description: Why it could not run: no-data, no-code, code-error, compute-infeasible, licence.

figure.description: Path to the regenerated figure, for visual comparison.

discrepancy.description: Present when the re-run disagreed with the document. Required detail for status `mismatch` and `partial`: what the document reported, what the re-run gave, and the likeliest cause. Without it a mismatch is an accusation with no argument.

kind.description: Where the disagreement comes from. `methodological-gap` means the two could differ legitimately — different exclusions, a different test — and the document is not thereby wrong.

relation.description:
Relation vocabulary. Directed unless marked symmetric. Converses are listed together: an exporter SHOULD emit the canonical direction and MAY emit both, and a consumer MUST tolerate both.

  entails        hypothesis/premise -> what follows from it        (converse: derived-from)
  derived-from   consequence -> what it follows from               (converse: entails)
  tests          prediction/result -> the claim it bears on        (neutral: does not say which way it came out)
  confirms       result -> the prediction it bore out
  refutes        result -> the prediction it contradicted
  supports       evidence -> the claim it makes more credible
  contradicts    either -> the other; they cannot both hold        (symmetric)
  requires       claim -> what it would be invalidated by          (converse: scopes)
  scopes         scope/bound -> what it bounds, or "*"            (converse: requires)
  validates      control -> the method or result it licenses
  rules-out      claim -> the alternative it eliminates
  enables-method method/resource -> what it made possible
  interprets     interpretation -> the result it reads
  extends        later or broader claim -> what it extends
  replicates     claim -> the earlier claim it reproduces
  part-of        component -> whole
  dissociates-with  two results whose contrast is itself the finding  (symmetric)
  qualifies      claim -> the claim it narrows without contradicting
  cites          claim -> a claim in another document

oneOf.description: Only for `scopes`: this claim bounds the whole set.

note.description: Why the relation holds. Load-bearing for `requires` and `dissociates-with`, where the reason is not recoverable from the two texts.

by.description: Who or what asserted the edge. Edges are inferred separately from claims and are the less reliable half.
